$comment: Per-role model ladder and effort level. ADR-0018 (ladder), ADR-0021 (effort).
One object per role so the two never drift apart: two maps keyed by role
would be a synchronization debt, and this file exists to be a single source.
ladder: ordered by preference. The guard runs the first rung that is not
rate-limited, per the ledger issue labeled model-limits. The LAST rung is
the floor: nothing below it is reachable, so an exhausted ladder means the
agent skips this cycle rather than silently dropping to a weaker model.
An empty ladder means no --model flag: action default, never falls back,
never skipped for model reasons.
The BDFL's rung is a budget decision, not a permission one. ADR-0031
gives the BDFL every role's model and effort choice under the standard
most capable this project can afford. Current choices are the data below;
the allowance incident that established the rule lives in issue #197.
effort: one of low, medium, high, xhigh, max, or empty for the
session default. Available levels depend on the model, which this file
cannot check; an unrecognized value is ignored with a log line rather than
failing the run.
thrift (issue #202): optional per-role ladder/effort override. Absent
means unchanged. agent-guard reads the allowance-state ledger issue
(written by agent-audit) and projects its week-average burn rate against
the next seven-day reset; when the projection misses the reset, it runs
this role at 'thrift' instead of its normal ladder/effort for that one
cycle. No file edit needed either direction: the guard re-projects on
every wake, so restoring the normal tier costs nothing once the
allowance shows slack again. Only roles worth thinning need an entry;
a role already on its floor model has nothing cheaper to fall back to.
The BDFL owns this file (ADR-0031). It lives outside .github/ so changing
it is an ordinary app-token commit, not an admin-PAT workflow push.

bdfl.$comment: Thrift suspended, operator directive (Telegram, 2026-10-03): speed up the director, slow down the rest, until the agent-system backlog (#486 et al.) is down. This seat was 47.3% of fleet cost already thrifted (SOURCES.md, 2026-09-19); running its full ladder uncapped raises that share further on purpose. The other roles need no edit to feel the other half of the order: the allowance projection is one shared reading, so a heavier bdfl burn tightens the discretionary keep_fraction (ADR-0039) for heartbeat/deslop/curator/herald/research on the next agent-audit cycle, same arithmetic, no cadence hand-pulled (the 2026-08-30 hand-pulls this replaced cost a run, a PR, a review and a worker deploy each, CLOCK comment in worker.js). Revisit: restore the thrift block below once the agent-system queue is clear; same falsification tell as before (a wake under ~20 turns posting nothing) would restore it sooner.

curator.$comment: Opus first, sonnet floor: adversarial critique is this seat's entire output, and weak sparring is noise that trains authors to ignore it (ADR-0044). One daily wake, so the raise costs one sonnet-to-opus delta a day; thrift sheds it first. Canary for claude-opus-5-5 (operator, Telegram, 2026-09-24), promoted 2026-09-27: run-telemetry.py's 2026-09-27 window shows 2 of 14 curator runs on claude-opus-5-5, no 404 in the model-availability ledger (#110) since the canary landed. Green, per its own falsification rule; promotes the herald, the researcher and the BDFL's third rung, all done this same run (SOURCES.md, 2026-09-27). Effort is pinned to high because Opus 5.5's own default is medium, one level below Opus 5's, and an empty value here would silently take that cut (SOURCES.md adoption log, 2026-09-24).

herald.$comment: Opus floor, no sonnet rung: writing quality for humans is this seat's entire output, and a weaker writer defeats the seat (ADR-0040). Thrift trades that deliberately when the alternative is a dead factory. claude-opus-5-5 promoted above claude-opus-5, same tier at 20% less per token: the curator's canary came back green (SOURCES.md, 2026-09-27).

researcher.$comment: Opus first: each research session is the fleet's judgment-densest, so the raise costs one sonnet-to-opus delta per session (operator directive, Telegram, 2026-09-01). Cadence moved off a fixed weekly wake to research-due's claim check (issue #541, operator request, Telegram, 2026-09-21), roughly twice weekly now, so this raise now costs about twice what it did when priced. claude-opus-5-5 promoted above claude-opus-5, same tier at 20% less per token: the curator's canary came back green (SOURCES.md, 2026-09-27).

reviewer.$comment: Sonnet held deliberately: highest session count in the fleet. The 2026-09-01 entry deferred this raise until #439 made per-seat burn share measurable; #439 shipped, and run-telemetry.py has published it since (site/agent-metrics.json). Priced 2026-09-19: 22.9% of fleet cost at a $0.71 median per run, the cheapest seat per run. The raise is now pricable and is deliberately not taken while the governor reads SLOW DOWN. SOURCES.md adoption log, 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-19.
